Extract the complete connected gray-and-muted-rose outlined curling ivy branch on the left, its two upper gold trefoil leaves, fine original hairlike tendrils, the small three-lobed gold cluster at its lower attachment, AND the blue-and-white trefoil flower within the curl: native inspection shows its painted tail joins the stem, so keep this connected ornament together. The blue and pale flower surfaces and pale highlights within the narrow stem stay opaque. Remove the broad gilt D letter stroke and orange border, ending the branch at its actual visible attachment without inventing a tip. Keep the entire selected original subject at its original proportions: every original fingertip, toe, petal fold, serration, thin stem, curl, feather, painted highlight and print hatching. Clear the unwanted page or flat painted background and every genuine opening between subject parts. Selected pale, gold, blue or white painted or engraved subject surfaces remain opaque. Remove neighboring unrelated subjects and printed page rules, lettering or captions. Preserve only source-visible parts, including original truncated ends; no invented hidden anatomy, new leaves, new tips, extended stalks, restored details or modern replacement artwork. Do not symmetrize, beautify, redraw, sharpen, stretch or compress the hand-drawn original. Fine natural antialiased contours without stepped polygon cuts or paper halos. Genuine transparent alpha outside and within the real openings, no rectangle or checkerboard paint.

retained_generated_ownership_guide.purpose: Retained AI alpha guide only; delivered opaque RGB belongs to the unchanged native source.

review.notes: Full untouched original page/regions, complete white/dark comparisons and native gilt-leaf detail inspected. Original pale folded-under leaf surfaces are opaque, complete stem contacts and original distal thin tendrils retained, genuine curled-stem openings clear. Glyph/contact serif fragments excluded. Exact native source RGB, hand-painted gold wear and original proportions retained; no invented leaf tips or rescaling.
